name: 29746-toppdecode-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), 256 streams, warmup the first 25% by completion, bounded at 1024 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix bucket: prompt exactly 1024 tokens, output exactly 1024 with `ignore_eos`, temperature 0.7 and top_p 0.8 on every request.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant generating full-page responses from page-length prompts for 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's launch arguments. Engine: commit a491b0911bf9d9ed264ec3ad83bdd9e96c0324a6
# (`git describe --tags` -> v0.11.1-404-ga491b0911b). Interpreter and hardware seal: configs/env.yaml.
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# ON by default on this engine, and off here as a validity condition: leaving it on makes how many
# prompt tokens are actually prefilled a function of arrival order and cache residency.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# This engine's own `vllm serve` defaults for a >=70 GiB non-A100 card, written down because a
# different launch path resolves a different pair. max-num-seqs MUST stay >= the 256 declared
# streams, or the sequence cap and not the load profile bounds how deep the running batch gets.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
max-model-len: 4096

# `enforce-eager` MUST STAY ABSENT: the engine is meant to run compiled and cudagraph-captured,
# as it does by default.
